_: THE SOURCE OF TRUTH FOR WHAT THE REPOSITORY GATES COVER. Every consumer DERIVES from
this file; none restates it. Reconciling two lists is not the fix - reconciled lists agree
JSON AND NOT TOML, ON A MEASURED CONSTRAINT RATHER THAN A PREFERENCE: the suite is
stdlib-only across a 3.9-3.13 CI matrix (check-overclaim.py states this in its own
docstring), and `tomllib` does not exist below 3.11. TOML would break the two oldest legs.
EVERY EXCLUSION CARRIES BOTH `reason` AND `remove_when`. An exclusion with only a reason is
a PERMANENT GRANT and the table becomes where claims go to stop being checked; with an
expiry condition the table is AUDITABLE, because an entry whose condition has since been
met is a stale exclusion findable by machine. Same discipline as a tombstone: a suppression
that carries its own expiry rather than a standing one.

scripts.reason: ruff-checked only; the mypy --strict typing sweep over sweep.py (~1,900 lines) plus three gate scripts is an unknown-sized job and is a separate boarded increment
scripts.remove_when: scripts/ passes mypy --strict and that increment merges

tests.reason: not strict-typed; test modules use unittest.mock and SimpleNamespace fixtures throughout

_gates_note: A WILDCARD GATE CANNOT DRIFT IN THE ROSTER DIRECTION AT ALL - its coverage follows from its
mechanism, so every tracked file is scanned by construction. Its honest failure mode is the
OPPOSITE one: a reader over-reading a green build. check-voice.py already states this in
prose ('a boundary the script states rather than implies, so a green build is never read as
"no first-person-plural anywhere"'). Recording the mode here promotes that convention from
a docstring to data, so the claim is checkable rather than merely written down.

.github.reason: CI configuration, not part of the reader-facing repository layout the README describes
.github.remove_when: the README's layout section is repurposed to describe infrastructure as well as source

hygiene.reason: the Repo hygiene job is two multi-line shell assertions embedded in the workflow YAML; it has NO single-line runnable command, so there is nothing for the README's 'Run the static gates' block to mirror
hygiene.remove_when: a local equivalent command exists (e.g. scripts/check-hygiene.py) and the README documents it

-v.reason: unittest verbosity: changes what the runner prints, never what it executes or asserts. CI wants per-test output; the README shows the plain command. Removed from BOTH sides before comparison, never one
-v.remove_when: neither the README claims region nor any CI command uses -v (the check reds on that state as stale)

_display_only_note: A FLAG LISTED HERE IS DELETED FROM BOTH SIDES BEFORE THE README AND CI ARE COMPARED, so this table
is a TRUST BOUNDARY the check does not close. Its mechanical staleness catches only an entry that
appears on NEITHER side. Adding a behavioural flag here (e.g. -W, which changes whether a warning
fails the run) while it sits on one side would normalise the #46 defect away and turn it green.
Only flags that change what is PRINTED belong here, and an edit to this table is visible in this

dissent-gate.yml.reason: the process gate: a pull_request_target job that judges a PR's Dissent-Ref line against the board. It has no command a reader runs locally (it needs a PR event and the board), so there is nothing for the README claims region to mirror. Its rules are tested offline by tests/test_dissent_gate.py and its workflow invariants (no head checkout, no cache, no interpolated run line, read-only permissions) are pinned there
dissent-gate.yml.remove_when: the README claims check partitions workflow files other than ci.yml, or the gate gains a locally runnable form that the README claims

_workflows_note: EVERY FILE UNDER .github/workflows/ IS EITHER PARTITIONED BY THE README CLAIMS CHECK (today only
ci.yml) OR LISTED IN workflows_excluded with a reason and a remove_when. An unlisted workflow file
is RED, and an entry naming a file that no longer exists is RED as stale. The table was absent at
P10a (an empty table satisfies every entry check vacuously, so exemption_tables() reds one); P10b
added it with its first entry, the process gate's own workflow.
_non_exemption_keys_note: EVERY TOP-LEVEL KEY IS EITHER AN EXEMPTION TABLE OR LISTED HERE, and both directions red. A table
derived by shape alone would silently drop a MALFORMED table (an entry missing `reason`) instead
of failing it - the validator excluding the input it exists to validate. And a key listed here
that no longer exists is a stale entry, redded like any other.
_exemptions_note: ⚠ KEYED ON CI JOB NAMES, AND THE KEYS ARE THEMSELVES PARTITIONED — which is the correction, not
a detail. Keying an exemption table on job names makes the table a CLAIM ABOUT ci.yml's JOB SET,
i.e. a second enumeration. An exemption naming a job that has since been renamed or deleted
would then be inert for exactly the reason the first version of this table was inert: an entry
nothing consults never fails, so it lapses SILENTLY while its presence still reads as evidence
So ci_exemption_errors partitions both ways: no job may be silently unchecked, and no exemption
may name a job that does not exist. That is what makes the claim honest - hygiene is exempt from
a check that WOULD otherwise fire, and renaming the job REDS rather than quietly lapsing.
EVERY ENTRY CARRIES `side`, WITH NO DEFAULT. side=ci keys a CI JOB and exempts that job's BLOCK
steps (or its absence of any run step) - nothing else; a runnable command in the same job must
still be claimed. It is stale when the job no longer exists or no longer has anything to exempt.
side=readme keys a README CLAIM with no CI counterpart; it is stale when the claim leaves the
region or CI starts running it. Any other side value is an entry no predicate reads: RED.
RESIDUAL, STATED: a side=ci exemption is BLANKET TRUST over whatever that job's block scalars run.
The checker does not look inside a block and must not be read as if it did. Bounded, not closed:
changing a block edits .github/, which the process gate routes through an admin ruling.
